content.title: TransUnion (TRU) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
content.summary: Shares of credit reporting company TransUnion (NYSE:TRU) jumped 5.5% in the afternoon session after the stock bounced back from a steep sell-off in the previous trading session, which was triggered by a competitor's move to challenge the credit reporting industry.

content.title: Selloff of Equifax, TransUnion, Experian Stocks Is Overdone. ‘Buy the Dip,’ Analysts Say.
content.summary: Shares of  Equifax TransUnion  and  Experian  dropped sharply Thursday after  Fair Isaac   unveiled new pricing models that will allow mortgage lenders to calculate and distribute FICO scores directly to borrowers.  The program would allow score resellers to bypass the credit bureaus, who currently charge a markup.  All three stocks pared their losses Friday, with  Equifax  rising 1.6%,  TransUnion  climbing 4.6%, and New York-listed Experian shares up 0.8%.

content.title: FICO Shakes Up Credit-Score Market
content.summary: FICO is upending the credit-scoring industry by giving mortgage lenders a way to offer its FICO credit score without dealing with Experian, Equifax or TransUnion.

content.title: FICO to Directly License Credit Scores to Mortgage Resellers
content.summary: Through a new program, mortgage resellers will be able to calculate and distribute credit scores directly to customers, reducing their reliance on credit bureaus.  This will bring more price transparency and savings for mortgage lenders, mortgage brokers and other industry participants, FICO said in a statement.  Shares of credit-reporting bureaus TransUnion and Equifax Inc. each fell more than 8% on Thursday.
